name: Learn several pool trick shots
blurb: Set-piece shots that look impossible and are mostly geometry plus a rehearsed setup. Four of them make you very good value at a pub table.
gear: Table access, ideally at quiet times
steps: Learn the fundamentals first — a reliable straight stroke is a prerequisite for every trick shot.
Learn a simple frozen-ball or combination shot where the setup does most of the work.
Learn a jump shot legally: an elevated cue striking downwards, never scooping under the ball.
Learn a masse or swerve shot to curve the cue ball around an obstructing ball.
Learn one multi-ball set piece that pots two or three balls at once.
Rehearse the setup precisely — trick shots depend on ball placement to the millimetre.
tips: Ask before attempting jump or masse shots on someone else’s table. Both can tear cloth if done badly.
Mark your setups with chalk dust while practising so you can reproduce them exactly.
proof: Four trick shots you can set up and land on demand, in front of people, first or second attempt.
